To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dry deposition fluxes of PFASs were estimated at Büsem located in northern German Coast, and their gas-particle partition coefficients were estimated using polyparameter linear free-energy relationships (PP-LFERS) model.
dry deposition fluxes of PFASs were dominated by gas deposition, and the gas deposition fluxes of the 12 neutral PFASs were mainly controlled by wind speed.

gas deposition of PFAs plays an important role during deposition to coastal ecosystem, and the polyparameter linear-free-energy relationship (PP-LFER) model can be used to estimate the gas/particle distribution coefficients of neutral PFAs.

the gas deposition of neutral PFASs was a significant pathway for PFASs deposition in marine ecosystem.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dry deposition of PFAS to marine ecosystem was mainly dominated by gas deposition, and the dry deposition of neutral PFASs could be estimated by employing PP-LFERs.
the gas deposition of PFAs played a key role on their dry deposition fluxes to marine ecosystem.

the dry deposition of PFAS to marine ecosystem was significant and the gas deposition played a key role in the total flux, and the PP-LFERs can reliably predict gas/particle partition coefficient of PFASs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dry deposition of neutral PFASs in coastal areas is dominated by gas-phase deposition, which is sensitive to wind speed and temperature, and the PP-LFERs are suitable for the estimation of gas/particle partition coefficient of neutral PFAS in the atmosphere.
gas deposition is an important pathway for PFASs to enter the marine ecosystem.
the dry deposition fluxes of atmospheric neutral PFOS, PFOA and PFNA are comparable to those of atmospheric neutral PCBs and PBDEs, which are known to have high deposition fluxes.
